title: Clear aligners
what: Aligners are clear trays that slowly move your teeth. Every 1 to 2 weeks, you switch to a new tray.
why: To straighten crooked teeth and fix the bite in adults and teens, when the orthodontist thinks aligners will work.
duration: treatment usually takes from a few months to 1 to 2 years; aligners are worn 20 to 22 hours a day

prepare.title: Treatment
prepare.text: Tooth decay and gum problems are treated first, and a cleaning is done.

prepare.title: X-rays
prepare.text: Usually a full-mouth X-ray is needed, sometimes a dental CT scan.

prepare.title: Commitment
prepare.text: Aligners work only if you wear them almost all the time.

bring: Dental X-rays, if you have them
steps: An orthodontist examines your teeth and orders X-rays
Your teeth are scanned or impressions are taken
A computer shows the plan for moving your teeth
Sometimes small bumps are bonded to the teeth to help the aligners grip
You get your first aligners and learn how to put them in
New aligners every 1 to 2 weeks, and visits on a schedule
feel: Each new aligner feels tight for the first 1 to 2 days
Your speech may change a little in the first days
after: Take the aligners out only to eat and to brush your teeth
After eating, brush your teeth, then put the aligners back in
Drink only water with the aligners in
After treatment, you need a retainer so your teeth do not move back

faq.q: Can I take the aligners out for a day?
faq.a: No. If you wear them less than 20 to 22 hours a day, the teeth move more slowly and treatment takes longer.
Hardly. Other people usually do not see them.

reminders.text: Orthodontist visit tomorrow. Brush your teeth and bring your aligners, if you already wear them.
